input_signals.name: PhysicalExpansionInNonInnovators
input_signals.expression: MUL(GROWTH(ppegt, 1), INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale)), -0.02))
input_signals.hypothesis: The negative return consequence of physical capacity expansion applies mainly to firms with negligible R&D intensity; for research-intensive firms, plant growth accompanies innovation commercialization and carries no such penalty.
input_signals.reasoning: The indicator switches on only when R&D-to-sales is below 2%, so the signal is capacity growth restricted to non-innovative firms and zero elsewhere, an explicitly conditional interaction rather than a blended score. Non-innovators expanding plant are the most likely to be chasing commoditized capacity with low marginal returns, so the negative slope should be steeper than for unconditional PPE growth.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( growth( ppegt, 1 ), indicator( neg( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ) ), -0.02 ) )

input_signals.name: TangibilityWeightedCapacityGrowth
input_signals.expression: MUL(GROWTH(ppegt, 1), RANK(RATIO(SUB(at, ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The return penalty for physical capacity expansion is proportional to how purely tangible the firm's capital base is; the same rate of plant growth carries no penalty when it sits on top of a large stock of booked and internally generated intangible capital.
input_signals.reasoning: Instead of averaging two anomaly legs, the expansion rate is multiplied by the firm's tangible-capital share rank, so the signal is large and positive only for fast-expanding, intangible-poor firms and mechanically collapses toward zero for fast-expanding, intangible-rich firms. This makes the intangible dimension a slope modifier on the investment effect rather than an additive second bet, and coalescing R&D and booked intangibles to zero keeps the non-reporting cohort in coverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( growth( ppegt, 1 ), rank( ratio( sub( at, add( coalesce( intan, 0 ), ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: ExternalCapitalRaisedByNonInnovators
input_signals.expression: MUL(RATIO(ADD(sstk, DELTA(dltt, 1)), at), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale))))
input_signals.hypothesis: External financing predicts low returns mainly when the firm has no intangible-investment program to justify the capital raise; issuance by R&D- and brand-building firms funds financially constrained intangible projects and should not be penalized.
input_signals.reasoning: The issuance intensity is multiplied by a continuous rank of intangible-spending deficit, so the signal loads only on capital raised by firms that spend nothing on knowledge or brand, making the intangible theme a slope modifier rather than a second additive anomaly leg. Both xrd and xad are coalesced to zero so the target cohort of non-reporters is retained, and the continuous weighting avoids the hard threshold used in the accepted capacity-growth signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ratio( add( sstk, delta( dltt, 1 ) ), at ), rank( neg( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), sale ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: InventoryBuildPerGrossProfit
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(invt, 1), SUB(sale, cogs)), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Physical working-capital expansion is only justified when the firm has intangible pricing power to sell the goods; firms accumulating inventory that is large relative to their gross profit lack product differentiation and will later face markdowns and demand disappointment.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the hiring channel and its contested sign, and instead scales a purely physical investment flow by gross profit, the accounting footprint of brand and product intangibles, so the same inventory build is penalized in commodity producers and tolerated in differentiated firms. Both tails are populated by real cohorts (over-stocking low-margin manufacturers versus high-margin firms with lean inventories), and the measure is a composition variable rather than a level of total investment, so it should not be neutralized by CMA.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( delta( invt, 1 ), sub( sale, cogs ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: NormalizedKnowledgeForPlantSubstitution
input_signals.expression: RATIO(SUB(DELTA(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 1), DELTA(ppent, 1)), ADD(ABS(DELTA(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 1)), ABS(DELTA(ppent, 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The direction in which a firm reallocates its marginal investment dollar — toward knowledge capital and away from net plant — is informative about future returns independently of the size of either flow, because the R&D leg is expensed and the plant leg is capitalized.
input_signals.reasoning: Dividing by the sum of absolute changes fixes the flagged scale problem directly: the index is bounded in [-1, 1] and gives the two channels equal weight, so its variance can no longer be dominated by the mechanically larger change in net PPE. It therefore measures substitution direction rather than being a sign-flipped physical-investment sort, and it is by construction close to scale- and industry-neutral.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( sub( delta( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 1 ), delta( ppent, 1 ) ), add( abs( delta( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 1 ) ), abs( delta( ppent, 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CapacityPushAgainstMarginErosion
input_signals.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))
input_signals.hypothesis: Capacity expansion is only justified when the product-market rents that intangible advantages generate are holding up; a firm pushing physical investment to the top of its own five-year range while its gross margin sits at the bottom of its own five-year range is expanding into a commoditizing business and will disappoint.
input_signals.reasoning: Both legs are within-firm time-series percentile positions, which removes the cross-sectional level of capex intensity and the cross-sectional level of gross profitability — precisely the two published anomaly components the critic identified in the ratio form — leaving only the timing interaction between capacity investment and margin erosion. Because the construct is a difference of two [0,1] own-history ranks, it is scale-, industry- and level-neutral, so it cannot be mechanically absorbed by CMA or RMW, and both tails are populated by real cohorts (expanding commoditizers versus retrenching margin-improvers).
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ts_rank( ratio( capx, ma( ppent, 3 ) ), 5 ), ts_rank( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 5 ) )

input_signals.name: KnowledgeVersusPlantInvestmentTiming
input_signals.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(xrd, MA(sale, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5))
input_signals.hypothesis: Among firms that run research programs, those currently at a five-year high in research intensity while physical investment sits at a five-year low are reallocating toward knowledge capital, and because the research leg is expensed while the retrenched capex leg reads as contraction, the market underreacts.
input_signals.reasoning: This applies the winning own-history-rank construction to the two investment channels directly, so both legs are [0,1] within-firm percentiles and neither dollar magnitude nor industry membership can dominate — the flaw that broke the earlier difference-in-changes substitution index. Using xrd uncoalesced deliberately restricts the sample to innovators, which removes the R&D-reporting-status contamination the critic identified in the peak-relative and count-based signals, so the sort is a genuine intra-firm reallocation test.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ts_rank( ratio( xrd, ma( sale, 3 ) ), 5 ), ts_rank( ratio( capx, ma( ppent, 3 ) ), 5 ) )

input_signals.name: InventoryBuildAgainstMarginErosion
input_signals.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(invt, MA(sale, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))
input_signals.hypothesis: Physical stock-building is only warranted when the firm's product differentiation is intact; a firm whose inventory relative to sales is at a five-year high precisely when its gross margin is at a five-year low is pushing goods into a market that is no longer paying for them, and future markdowns follow.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves the winning timing-contrast construction to the working-capital channel, which was the other flow signal with a real FMB slope (InventoryBuildPerGrossProfit, fmb −3.0), while eliminating the objection that a level ratio of capex to gross profit is a mechanical quotient of two published anomalies — both legs here are own-history ranks, so cross-sectional inventory intensity and cross-sectional gross profitability are differenced out. Testing plant and inventory under identical construction tells us whether the mechanism is capacity-specific or a general physical-overexpansion-into-commoditization effect.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ts_rank( ratio( invt, ma( sale, 3 ) ), 5 ), ts_rank( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 5 ) )

input_signals.name: LaborProductivityGainWithoutCapitalDeepening
input_signals.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(sale, emp), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(ppent, emp), 5))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose revenue per employee is climbing to own-history highs without any corresponding deepening of physical capital per employee are generating output from intangible sources — process knowledge, brand, software, organizational capital — and this unrecorded capital formation is underpriced.
input_signals.reasoning: This introduces the labor channel, which the archive has never successfully used, and frames intangible capital formation as productivity that appears without capital deepening rather than as reported R&D, so it is defined for non-R&D-reporting firms and escapes the reporting-status contamination that has weakened several earlier signals. Both legs are own-history ranks on the same employee base, so the signal is scale-, industry- and level-neutral by construction.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ts_rank( ratio( sale, emp ), 5 ), ts_rank( ratio( ppent, emp ), 5 ) )

input_signals.name: JointCapacityAndInventoryOvercommitment
input_signals.expression: SUB(MIN(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(invt, MA(sale, 3)), 5)), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))
input_signals.hypothesis: Physical over-commitment is only decisive when it happens in both channels at once: a firm simultaneously at own-history highs in fixed-capacity reinvestment and in inventory relative to sales, while its gross margin sits at an own-history low, is expanding a business whose intangible pricing power is disappearing.
input_signals.reasoning: Replacing the additive stack with MIN of the two physical legs implements the conjunction the hypothesis actually states — the signal is high only if capacity *and* inventory commitment are both elevated — and the margin leg now enters exactly once, so the construction is no longer dominated by own-history margin reversal. This is a functional-form change rather than a recombination: firms high on only one physical channel are pulled down to their weaker leg instead of being averaged into the top bucket.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( min( ts_rank( ratio( capx, ma( ppent, 3 ) ), 5 ), ts_rank( ratio( invt, ma( sale, 3 ) ), 5 ) ), ts_rank( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 5 ) )

input_signals.name: SlowMovingCapacityOvercommitment
input_signals.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(capx, 3), MA(ppent, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 3), 5))
input_signals.hypothesis: Over-commitment to physical capacity in the face of eroding product-market rents is a multi-year state rather than a single-year coincidence: firms whose three-year cumulative capacity spending is at an own-history high while their three-year average gross margin is at an own-history low are the ones that will disappoint.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the cumulative capex-versus-R&D stack the critic rejected as two published anomalies added together, and instead isolates a specific design choice on the archive's best signal — measurement horizon — by smoothing both legs to three years while keeping the own-history-rank machinery. If the horizon-smoothed version strengthens the alpha and Sharpe, the mechanism is persistent strategic over-commitment; if it weakens, the effect is genuinely a one-year timing coincidence, and either outcome sharpens the remaining generations at full coverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ts_rank( ratio( ts_sum( capx, 3 ), ma( ppent, 3 ) ), 5 ), ts_rank( ma( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 3 ), 5 ) )

input_signals.name: CapacityAdditionAgainstRentYieldOnPlant
input_signals.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), MA(ppent, 3)), 5))
input_signals.hypothesis: Capacity additions destroy value when each existing unit of plant is generating unusually little gross profit: the rent yield on physical capacity, which is determined by intangible advantages such as brand, product design and process knowledge, tells the firm whether more plant is worth building.
input_signals.reasoning: This repairs both flagged defects: the second leg is now gross profit per unit of plant, an explicitly intangible-rent measure built from sale and cogs, so the signal is genuinely cross-theme, and the investment leg is scaled by average assets rather than by plant, so heavy capex no longer mechanically raises one leg while depressing the other. It is distinct from the archived margin-timing signal because it conditions on the *level of rents earned per unit of capacity* rather than on the margin rate, separating rent scarcity from price erosion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ts_rank( ratio( capx, ma( at, 3 ) ), 5 ), ts_rank( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), ma( ppent, 3 ) ), 5 ) )

input_signals.name: RentPerWorkerVersusCapitalPerWorker
input_signals.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), emp), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(ppent, emp), 5))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose gross profit per employee is climbing to own-history highs without any deepening of plant per employee are earning rents from organizational and knowledge capital that never appears on the balance sheet, and this unrecorded capital formation is underpriced.
input_signals.reasoning: The accepted labor signal produced a strong cross-sectional slope (fmb 3.57) but no alpha, which is the signature of a revenue-scale confound; replacing revenue per worker with *gross profit* per worker isolates rent generation rather than sales volume, and gross profitability is the margin concept that has driven every successful signal in this archive. This is a single, targeted scaling change that identifies whether the labor channel's information is about intangible rents or merely about growth.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ts_rank( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), emp ), 5 ), ts_rank( ratio( ppent, emp ), 5 ) )

input_signals.name: TotalPhysicalCommitmentAgainstMarginErosion
input_signals.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(capx, DELTA(invt, 1)), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))
input_signals.hypothesis: The economically relevant quantity is total dollars committed to physical assets — new plant plus incremental inventory — relative to the firm's size, and committing an own-history-high share of assets to hard assets while gross margin is at an own-history low predicts low returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive contains a rank-conjunction of the capacity and inventory channels (MIN form, alpha −2.3%) but never their economically natural dollar sum, which weights each channel by how much capital it actually absorbs rather than by percentile position and avoids the double-counted margin leg the critic rejected. Scaling by average assets rather than by plant also breaks the shared-denominator artifact present in the capex-over-plant leg, so this is a substantive measurement improvement rather than a recombination.

input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ts_rank( ratio( add( capx, delta( invt, 1 ) ), ma( at, 3 ) ), 5 ), ts_rank( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 5 ) )

input_signals.name: OvercommitmentFundedFromOutsideCapital
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(sstk, DELTA(dltt, 1)), ADD(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Capacity expansion into eroding margins is destructive specifically when the money comes from outside investors rather than from the firm's own cash generation, because external funding severs the discipline that a shrinking rent base would otherwise impose on the investment decision.
input_signals.reasoning: Two changes address the critique: the financing leg is now a *funding-mix ratio* — outside capital raised per dollar of total investment spending, including the knowledge-investment channel — rather than an issuance level, so it is not the net-external-financing anomaly in disguise, and the legs are combined with MIN so the signal fires only under the joint condition the hypothesis specifies. Both legs are cross-sectional ranks in [0,1], and winsorizing the funding ratio controls the small-denominator tail for firms with negligible investment.

input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5))), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), MA(sale, 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The long side of the theme is the mirror image of the short side: firms whose gross margins are at own-history highs while physical capital commitment is at own-history lows, and which carry a strong research base relative to peers, are compounding intangible advantage without absorbing capital, and this is underpriced.
input_signals.reasoning: Every strong result in this archive is on the short side, and the positive-signed candidates (PeakRelative at t 1.78, KnowledgeVersusPlantTiming with no alpha) were never given the gating structure that made the short side work, so this tests whether the conjunction mechanism is symmetric or whether the effect is purely a distress/over-commitment phenomenon. It keeps full coverage through the zero-R&D convention and the industry-relative endowment gate, so a positive result would not be a repackaged R&D-intensity sort.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( sub( ts_rank( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 5 ), ts_rank( ratio( capx, ma( ppent, 3 ) ), 5 ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), ma( sale, 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CapacityPushIntoDeterioratingRentTrend
input_signals.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: What matters for capacity decisions is the direction in which the firm's intangible pricing power is moving, not merely where the current margin sits in its own history: committing capital while the five-year margin trend is steeply negative signals expansion into structural competitive decline.
input_signals.reasoning: Every successful signal in the archive uses the *position* of the margin in its own five-year history, which conflates cyclical dips with structural erosion; substituting a five-year fitted margin trend tests whether the mechanism is about direction of decline, and if so this variant should improve both the slope and the alpha because it removes mean-reverting margin noise from the gate. The capex leg stays as an own-history rank so no cross-sectional investment level enters, keeping the construct outside CMA's span.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ts_rank( ratio( capx, ma( ppent, 3 ) ), 5 ), rank( neg( trend( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: NetHardAssetCommitmentAgainstMarginErosion
input_signals.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))
input_signals.hypothesis: What is punished is hard-asset accumulation *net of* knowledge accumulation: a firm putting an own-history-high share of its asset base into plant beyond what it spends on research, precisely while gross margin sits at an own-history low, is deepening a commoditizing business instead of renewing its advantage.
input_signals.reasoning: Rather than smoothing an existing gate, this moves the intangible channel inside the commitment measure itself: the investment leg is now a signed tangible-minus-knowledge spending balance, so the same firm is scored differently depending on whether its capex is accompanied by research, which is the theme's mechanism expressed continuously rather than as an extreme-cohort intersection. It keeps full coverage through the zero-R&D convention, scales by average assets so the two channels are commensurable, and remains a within-firm timing contrast that no cross-sectional investment factor spans.

input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ts_rank( ratio( sub( capx, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), ma( at, 3 ) ), 5 ), ts_rank( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 5 ) )

input_signals.expression: MUL(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5)), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), MA(sale, 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Knowledge endowment amplifies the return consequences of capital-allocation timing in both directions: among research-rich firms, capital restraint with margin repair is strongly rewarded and capacity pushing into margin erosion is strongly punished, while research-poor firms show a muted response either way.

input_signals.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(ACCEL(RATIO(SUB(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MA(at, 3))), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))
